title: Building materials
summary: Nominal versus real sizes for lumber, plywood, OSB, steel, PVC and copper pipe, plus sheet metal gauges. Also gives bag yields, mix ratios and curing times for concrete and mortar.

steps.text: Measure the real piece first. Lumber, panels and pipe are sold by nominal size, not true size.
Use the tables to match a nominal size to its true size in inches and millimetres.
For concrete, pick a bag size, work out bags per square metre or cubic metre, then follow the curing times.
steps.warn: Wet concrete burns skin and eyes. Wear gloves, eye protection and an N95 or better for dry mix.

steps.text: For anything that carries load, follow local building codes and ask an inspector or engineer if you can reach one.

notes:
Nominal sizes are names, not measurements. Measure the real piece with a tape or calipers. For anything that carries load, follow local building codes, and ask a building inspector or engineer if you can reach one. (Quikrete)

## Lumber: nominal and actual
Rule of thumb: subtract 1/4 in for nominal sizes under 2 in, 1/2 in for sizes under 8 in, and 3/4 in for larger. Sizes are for dry, planed softwood. (Engineering ToolBox)

| Nominal (in) | Actual (in) | Actual (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 x 4 | 3/4 x 3-1/2 | 19 x 89 |
| 2 x 4 | 1-1/2 x 3-1/2 | 38 x 89 |
| 2 x 6 | 1-1/2 x 5-1/2 | 38 x 140 |
| 2 x 8 | 1-1/2 x 7-1/4 | 38 x 184 |
| 2 x 10 | 1-1/2 x 9-1/4 | 38 x 235 |
| 2 x 12 | 1-1/2 x 11-1/4 | 38 x 286 |
| 4 x 4 | 3-1/2 x 3-1/2 | 89 x 89 |

## Plywood and OSB
- Standard sheet: 1220 x 2440 mm (4 x 8 ft). (APA)
- Common Canadian plywood sheathing thicknesses (metric nominal) are 9.5, 12.5, 15.5, 18.5 and 25.5 mm, about 3/8, 1/2, 5/8, 3/4 and 1 in. One maker lists its 12.5, 15.5 and 18.5 mm panels with US labels of 15/32, 19/32 and 23/32 in. (Tolko)
- OSB (CSA O325), 1220 x 2440 mm sheet: (CWC)

| Thickness | Weight of one sheet |
|---|---|
| 9.5 mm (3/8 in) | 18 kg (40 lb) |
| 11 mm (7/16 in) | 21 kg (46 lb) |
| 12 mm (15/32 in) | 23 kg (50 lb) |
| 15 mm (19/32 in) | 29 kg (63 lb) |
| 18 mm (23/32 in) | 34 kg (76 lb) |
| 22 mm (7/8 in) | 42 kg (92 lb) |

- Both 12.0 mm (15/32 in) and 12.7 mm (1/2 in) OSB are made, so measure. (APA)
- A span rating such as 24/16 gives the largest recommended spacing of supports, in inches, centre to centre. The left number is for roofs, the right for floors, with the panel's long side across the supports. (APA)

## Pipe: nominal size is not the outside diameter
Steel and PVC pipe share the same outside diameter (OD) for each nominal size. Copper tube is different: its OD is 1/8 in larger than its nominal size. (Engineering ToolBox, Westlake)

| Nominal | Steel / PVC OD | PVC Sch 40 inside | Copper tube OD |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1/2 in | 0.840 in (21.3 mm) | 0.622 in | 0.625 in (15.9 mm) |
| 3/4 in | 1.050 in (26.7 mm) | 0.824 in | 0.875 in (22.2 mm) |
| 1 in | 1.315 in (33.4 mm) | 1.049 in | 1.125 in (28.6 mm) |
| 1-1/4 in | 1.660 in (42.2 mm) | 1.380 in | 1.375 in (34.9 mm) |
| 1-1/2 in | 1.900 in (48.3 mm) | 1.610 in | 1.625 in (41.3 mm) |
| 2 in | 2.375 in (60.3 mm) | 2.067 in | 2.125 in (54.0 mm) |
| 3 in | 3.500 in (88.9 mm) | 3.068 in | - |
| 4 in | 4.500 in (114.3 mm) | 4.026 in | - |

Schedule 80 PVC has the same OD but a thicker wall, so a smaller bore. (Westlake)

## Concrete
- Old rule of thumb by volume: 1 cement : 2 sand : 3 gravel. Too much water weakens it. (U Illinois)
- Bagged mix: add about 2.8 to 4.3 L of water per 36.2 kg (80 lb) bag. Pour 50 mm (2 in) thick or more. (Quikrete)

| Bag | Yield | Bags per m³ | Covers at 100 mm (4 in) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18.1 kg (40 lb) | 8.5 L | 118 | 0.085 m² (0.9 ft²) |
| 27.2 kg (60 lb) | 12.7 L | 79 | 0.13 m² (1.35 ft²) |
| 36.2 kg (80 lb) | 17 L | 59 | 0.17 m² (1.8 ft²) |

Yields are Quikrete's; bags per m³ and coverage are worked out from them. Half the thickness covers twice the area. A 30 kg bag yields about 14 L (scaled by weight); check the bag. One cubic metre poured 100 mm thick covers 10 m². Set Quikrete mix weighs about 2,240 kg/m³. (Quikrete)

**Curing:** keep it damp for 5 days at 21 °C or warmer, 7 days at 10 to 21 °C. Protect from freezing for the first 48 hours. Hot, dry or windy weather dries it too fast and can cause shrinkage cracks. (Quikrete) The longer it stays moist, the stronger it gets. (ACA) Typical 7-day strength 17.2 MPa (2,500 psi), 28-day 27.5 MPa (4,000 psi) for that bagged mix. (Quikrete)

**Safety:** wet concrete burns skin and eyes. Wear nitrile gloves, eye protection and, for dry mix, an N95 or better respirator: cement and sand dust holds silica. (Quikrete, CCOHS)

## Mortar (by volume, cement : lime : sand)

| Type | Typical mix | Min strength | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| M | 1 : 1/4 : 3 | 17.2 MPa (2,500 psi) | High strength, stiff to work |
| S | 1 : 1/2 : 4-1/2 | 12.4 MPa (1,800 psi) | Stronger all-purpose |
| N | 1 : 1 : 6 | 5.2 MPa (750 psi) | Normal use, most brick |
| O | 1 : 2 : 9 | 2.4 MPa (350 psi) | Interior, repointing old work |

Ratios and strengths: (Engineering ToolBox). Use: (BIA). Measure by volume, with sand damp and loose. (BIA)

## Sheet metal gauge (mm)
Higher gauge = thinner. The same number gives a different thickness in each metal. Real sheet varies by tolerance. (Metal Supermarkets)

| Gauge | Mild steel | Galvanised | Stainless | Aluminium |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 3.42 | 3.51 | 3.57 | 2.59 |
| 12 | 2.66 | 2.75 | 2.78 | 2.05 |
| 14 | 1.90 | 1.99 | 1.98 | 1.63 |
| 16 | 1.52 | 1.61 | 1.59 | 1.29 |
| 18 | 1.21 | 1.31 | 1.27 | 1.02 |
| 20 | 0.91 | 1.01 | 0.95 | 0.81 |
| 22 | 0.76 | 0.85 | 0.79 | 0.64 |
| 24 | 0.61 | 0.70 | 0.64 | 0.51 |
| 26 | 0.45 | 0.55 | 0.48 | 0.41 |

Mild steel in inches: 10 ga 0.1345, 12 ga 0.1046, 14 ga 0.0747, 16 ga 0.0598, 18 ga 0.0478, 20 ga 0.0359. (Metal Supermarkets)
